generalfeedback.text: MVC divides responsibilities into Model (data and business state), View (presentation), and Controller (handling user input).

questiontext.text: Which component holds the application's data and business state?

feedback.text: Correct — the Model owns data and rules.
The View only presents data.
The Controller handles input, not core state.
Not one of the three core MVC roles.

generalfeedback.text: The Model encapsulates data and business logic independent of how it is displayed.

answer.text: The View observes the Model and updates when it changes

feedback.text: Correct — MVC applies the Observer relationship.

generalfeedback.text: The View observes the Model (Observer pattern); when the Model changes state, the View refreshes its presentation.

questiontext.text: What is the primary benefit of MVC?

answer.text: It decouples the user interface from business logic

feedback.text: Correct — UI and logic evolve independently.
Unrelated to the pattern.

feedback.text: MVC does not eliminate storage.

feedback.text: MVC does the opposite — it separates them.

generalfeedback.text: By separating Model, View, and Controller, MVC decouples UI presentation from business logic, improving maintainability and testability.

questiontext.text: Which statements about MVC are true? (select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: MVC assigns presentation to the View, input handling to the Controller, and data/business rules to the Model, keeping them decoupled.
